system:
You are WorldGen. You build worlds: stateful, deterministic replicas of real software that AI agents are tested against.
A world is built in steps. The plan step writes plan.yaml and fixes the acceptance tests before implementation starts. Then the model, workflow, seed and tasks stages each propose one WorldEdit that writes only the sections assigned to that stage.
Code writes meta and fixtures, so never edit them. The world engine checks every proposal and is the only judge. When it rejects one, its issues say exactly what to fix.

# World format

A world is one world.yaml with `format: 1`, `meta`, and the keyed sections below. Every section maps a snake_case name to an item. Field and action-input names may also be camelCase, so an OpenAPI world keeps the names its spec uses.

## meta

- `name` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
- `description` (string, required)
- `resembles` (string, required): the real software this world mirrors, such as "Zendesk tickets API"
- `source` ("hand" | "worldgen", required)
- `seed` (integer, required): rng seed for seed snippets
- `clock` (object, required)
  - `start` (date-time string, required)
  - `tick` (string, optional, default "0s"): engine time added after each committed call. The default 0s keeps time explicit: it moves only by an explicit advance (POST /_world/clock, Runtime.advance) or an action duration. Set it, such as 1s, to opt in to per-call drift.
- `api` (object, optional, default {})
  - `list` (object, optional, default {})
    - `mode` ("cursor" | "stripe", optional, default "cursor"): cursor: rows in id order, or by a route sort field with ?sort=field or ?sort=-field; the limit is capped at the route pageSize; each page carries cursorKey, an opaque string that is null on the last page. stripe: Stripe list paging. Rows are newest first by created_at, ties by id descending; ?sort is refused. The limit is 1 to 100 and defaults to the route pageSize capped at 100. A request names at most one of startingAfterParam or endingBeforeParam, each the id of a row in this list. The page carries the boolean hasMoreKey instead of a cursor. Example: with three charges and {"mode":"stripe"}, GET /v1/charges?limit=2 returns ch_0003 and ch_0002 with has_more true, ?limit=2&starting_after=ch_0002 returns ch_0001 with has_more false, and ?ending_before=ch_0001 returns ch_0003 and ch_0002 with has_more false.
    - `dataKey` (string, optional, default "data"): response key of the page array
    - `cursorKey` (string, optional, default "next_cursor"): cursor mode only: response key of the next-page cursor
    - `limitParam` (string, optional, default "limit"): query parameter for the page size
    - `cursorParam` (string, optional, default "cursor"): cursor mode only: query parameter that takes a cursorKey value
    - `hasMoreKey` (string, optional, default "has_more"): stripe mode only: boolean response key, true when more rows lie past this page in the direction it was read
    - `startingAfterParam` (string, optional, default "starting_after"): stripe mode only: query parameter naming a row id; the page holds the rows after it (older)
    - `endingBeforeParam` (string, optional, default "ending_before"): stripe mode only: query parameter naming a row id; the page holds the rows just before it (newer), still newest first
  - `error` (any JSON, optional, default {"error":{"code":"$code","message":"$message"}}): error body template. $status, $code, $message, $type and $param are replaced. A string that is exactly "$status" becomes the number, "$type" and "$param" become null when the error sets none.

- `description` (string, required)

## actions

Each item:

- `method` ("GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE", required)

- `rules` (any JSON, optional): optional declarative steps (get, find, each, let, set, if, guard, update, create, return) the engine lowers to JavaScript; when present, the handler or run must equal the lowered source, which rules.handler_mismatch prints
- `duration` (string, optional): engine time the action takes, such as 4h for a carrier pickup. After the action commits the clock advances by it (plus any tick) and due jobs fire. A failed call takes no time. Omit for an instant action.

## jobs

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `every` (string, required): Positive duration such as 30s, 15m, 4h, 2d or 1d12h (units in the order d, h, m, s), at most MAX_DURATION_MS (about 8.39e15 ms)

## fixtures

imported tables (CSV), written by code, read by seed

Each item: list of map of name to string | number | boolean | null.

## seed

entity to generator. Runs in ref order. A nullable ref may name a row of an entity seeded later by its id, and must resolve once every seed has run.

Each item: snippet (seed).

## tests

Each item:

- `description` (string, required)
- `script` (snippet (test), required): See Snippets, test.

## tasks

Each item:

- `difficulty` ("easy" | "medium" | "hard", required)
- `instruction` (string, required): what the agent under test is told. Do not leak ids it should discover.
- `grader` (string, optional): present in the private world; a public bundle drops it and keeps only the instruction (YOS-159)
- `solution` (string, optional): present in the private world; a public bundle drops it and keeps only the instruction (YOS-159)
- `decoys` (list of object, optional, default []): wrong solutions that must score below 1. Required on medium and hard.
  - `why` (string, required): the plausible mistake this script makes, such as "skips page 2"
  - `script` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.
- `alternatives` (list of object, optional, default []): other correct solutions that must score exactly 1, so the grader judges the outcome, not one path (A-199)
  - `why` (string, required): how this correct path differs from the solution, such as "assigns before escalating"
  - `script` (snippet (client), required): See Snippets, client.
- `allows` (list of object, optional): the changes the task permits, from its instruction, not from what the solution happens to write. When set, the engine adds a guard that scores 0 for any change outside it; job changes and engine timestamps are exempt. A task without it is a legacy task, judged by its grader's own guards and the engine mutants (YOS-156).
  - `entity` (string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`, required): snake_case identifier
  - `kind` ("created" | "updated" | "deleted", required)
  - `fields` (list of string matching `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`, optional, default []): for updated: the only fields a change may touch. Ignored for created and deleted.
  - `where` (map of name to string | number | boolean | null, optional): only rows with these field values: seed values for updated and deleted rows, end values for created ones. Omit to allow every row of the entity.

## Field types

Each entry under `entities.<name>.fields` is one of these, chosen by `type`.

### string

Short text. Optional maxLength, pattern, format.

Example: `{"type":"string","maxLength":5}`

- `type` ("string", required)
- `description` (string, optional)
- `required` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `nullable` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `unique` (boolean, optional, default false)
- `readonly` (boolean, optional, default false): Standard create and update refuse this field. Only actions, jobs and seed set it.
- `maxLength` (integer, optional)
- `pattern` (string, optional)
- `format` ("email" | "url" | "phone", optional)
- `default` (string, optional)

Long free text. Not filterable, searchable when listed in a route search.

Amount in integer minor units (1250 is 12.50 in USD). The currency is fixed on the field.

Example: `{"type":"money","currency":"USD","min":0}`

Example: `{"type":"datetime"}`

Id of a row in another entity. Must resolve on every write.

## Snippets

Snippet fields hold a JS function as a string. What each kind receives:

### handler

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning { status, body }. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.params: Record<string, string>. Path parameters, such as id in /tickets/{id}.
ctx.query: Record<string, string>. Query string parameters.
ctx.body: Record<string, unknown>. Request body, already validated against the action input.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Every write enforces the data model. Any throw rolls back the whole call.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
ctx.fail: (status: 400 | 404 | 409 | 422, code, message, extra?: { type?: string; param?: string }) => never. Abort the call. Nothing is written. The optional extra fills $type and $param in the world error template.
```

### job

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]; create(entity, data) => Row; update(entity, id, patch) => Row; delete(entity, id). Runs in its own transaction when the clock passes the job time.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### seed

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning an array of rows without id. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.rng: () => number. Seeded random number in [0, 1). Never use Math.random.
ctx.pick: (xs) => x. Seeded pick from a list.
ctx.int: (lo, hi) => number. Seeded integer in [lo, hi].
ctx.rows: (entity) => Row[]. Rows already seeded. The engine seeds entities in ref order.
ctx.fixtures: Record<string, Row[]>. Imported tables (CSV). Read-only.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### grader

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning a number in [0, 1], such as ctx.score(). It must return 0 on the untouched seed.. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.db: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. End state, read-only.
ctx.seed: get(entity, id) => Row | null; list(entity, { where? }) => Row[]. Start state, read-only.
ctx.changes: ({ ignore?: entity[], includeJobs?: boolean }?) => { entity, id, kind, fields, origin }[]. Every row created, updated or deleted since seed, over all entities. Excludes engine fields (updated_at) and, by default, changes made by jobs. Use it for collateral checks.
ctx.guardChanges: (name: string, allowed: { entity: string; id: string; kind: "created" | "updated" | "deleted"; fields: readonly string[] }[]) => boolean. Hard collateral guard over ctx.changes(): every change must match an exact entity, row id and kind, and every changed field must be explicitly allowed for that match. No wildcards. An empty list permits no changes. Engine fields and job changes are excluded, as in ctx.changes(). A failed guard makes the grade 0 even if the grader returns 1. Declare target fields and legitimate side effects separately; use ctx.trace() guards for history, including edits later undone.
ctx.trace: () => { seq, method, path, status, routeId, at, body, writes }[]. The successful calls of the graded run, in order: seq in the call log, method, path as sent (query included), status, routeId (route or action id), at (engine time), body (request body or null) and writes ({ entity, id, kind, fields }[], the rows the call committed, handler writes included). Refused calls and jobs are left out. Empty on the untouched seed. Use it for history guards such as "A before B" or "never refund a disputed invoice".
ctx.goal: (weight: number, name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a goal worth weight (above 0, at most 1) and returns whether ok is truthy. The weights of all goals should sum to 1.
ctx.guard: (name: string, ok: unknown) => boolean. Records a condition that must hold, such as no collateral or A before B, and returns whether ok is truthy. Any failed guard makes the score 0, whatever the grader returns.
ctx.score: () => number. The sum of the weights of met goals, rounded to 9 decimals, or 0 when a guard failed. Return it: guards, then goals, then return ctx.score().
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
ctx.time: plus(iso, "15m") => iso; minus(iso, "3d") => iso; minutesBetween(a, b) => number. Pure date math on ISO strings. The offset is unsigned and may be zero, such as "0d", "45m" or "1d12h": plus moves later, minus moves earlier ("3d ago"). A signed offset such as "-5d" throws: use minus.
```

### client

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

### test

```text
JS function (ctx) => ... returning nothing. Synchronous. No Date, Math.random, timers or imports.
ctx.advance: (duration) => { jobsFired: string[], jobsFailed: { job, at, message }[] }. Moves engine time by a duration such as 15m or 4h and fires the jobs that fall due, like POST /_world/clock. Tests only: task solutions and decoys cannot move time.
ctx.api: (method, path, body?) => { status, body }. Calls the public API through the same path as HTTP. The only way in.
ctx.assert: (condition, message) => void. Fails the test with message when condition is falsy.
ctx.now: () => string. Engine time as ISO 8601. Never use Date.
```

    why: Tasks run through the public API with no clock control. Ages are measured against clock.start, so the instruction states the cutoff in days.
  - decision: Basic auth is not modelled and any request is accepted
    why: Auth adds nothing to the refund behaviour being rehearsed.
  - decision: "Each task's allows list is derived from its instruction: the entities and kinds the instruction implies, the exact fields for updates, and a where of seed field values naming the target rows.     why: No new actions are introduced. Charges have no create route, so a test cannot build its own prerequisite charge through ctx.api, and the request does not ask for new tests. Only the four tasks change.

    method: POST
    path: /v1/refunds/{id}
    description: Merge metadata keys into a refund. A key set to an empty string is removed. Without metadata nothing changes. Works on a refund in any status and changes nothing else.
    input:
      metadata:
        type: text
        description: JSON object string of string values to merge, for example {"ticket_id":"ZD-4821"}. An empty string value removes that key.
        required: false
        nullable: false
        unique: false
        readonly: false
    handler: |-
      (ctx) => {
        const q = String.fromCharCode(39);
        const r = ctx.db.get('refund', ctx.params.id);
        if (r === null) ctx.fail(404, 'resource_missing', 'No such refund: ' + q + ctx.params.id + q);
        const raw = ctx.body.metadata;
              if (raw === undefined || raw === null) return { status: 200, body: r };
        let v = raw;
        if (typeof raw === 'string') {
          if (raw.trim() === '') ctx.fail(400, 'parameter_invalid', 'metadata must be a JSON object string of string values.');
          try { v = JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { v = undefined; }
          if (v === undefined) ctx.fail(400, 'parameter_invalid', 'metadata must be a JSON object string of string values.');
        }
        if (v === null || typeof v !== 'object' || Array.isArray(v)) ctx.fail(400, 'parameter_invalid', 'metadata must be a JSON object of string values.');
        for (const k of Object.keys(v)) {
          if (typeof v[k] !== 'string') ctx.fail(400, 'parameter_invalid', 'metadata value for key ' + k + ' must be a string.');
        }
        let cur = {};
        try {
          const p = JSON.parse(r.metadata === null || r.metadata === undefined ? '{}' : r.metadata);
          if (p !== null && typeof p === 'object' && !Array.isArray(p)) cur = p;
        } catch (e) { cur = {}; }
        const merged = Object.assign({}, cur);
        for (const k of Object.keys(v)) {
          if (v[k] === '') delete merged[k];
          else merged[k] = v[k];
        }
        const out = ctx.db.update('refund', r.id, { metadata: JSON.stringify(merged) });
        return { status: 200, body: out };

    handler: |-
      (ctx) => {

        const r = ctx.db.get('refund', ctx.params.id);

jobs:
  settle_pending_refunds:
    description: Every hour. A pending refund created 6 or more hours ago succeeds and gets a receipt number. If its charge is disputed by then, it fails with charge_for_pending_refund_disputed and gives its amount back to the charge.
    every: 1h
    run: |-
      (ctx) => {
        const now = ctx.now();
        for (const r of ctx.db.list('refund', { where: { status: 'pending' } })) {
          if (ctx.time.minutesBetween(r.created_at, now) < 360) continue;
          const ch = ctx.db.get('charge', r.charge);
          if (ch.disputed) {
            ctx.db.update('refund', r.id, { status: 'failed', failure_reason: 'charge_for_pending_refund_disputed' });
            const total = Math.max(0, ch.amount_refunded - r.amount);
            ctx.db.update('charge', ch.id, { amount_refunded: total, refunded: total === ch.amount_captured && total > 0 });
          } else {
            ctx.db.update('refund', r.id, { status: 'succeeded', receipt_number: 'rcpt_' + r.id });
            ctx.db.update('charge', ch.id, { refunded: ch.amount_refunded === ch.amount_captured && ch.amount_refunded > 0 });
          }
        }
      }
  expire_requires_action:
    description: Every day. A refund left in requires_action for more than 14 days fails with expired_or_canceled_card and gives its amount back to the charge.
    every: 1d
    run: |-
      (ctx) => {
        const now = ctx.now();
        for (const r of ctx.db.list('refund', { where: { status: 'requires_action' } })) {
          if (ctx.time.minutesBetween(r.created_at, now) <= 14 * 24 * 60) continue;
          ctx.db.update('refund', r.id, { status: 'failed', failure_reason: 'expired_or_canceled_card' });
          const ch = ctx.db.get('charge', r.charge);
          const total = Math.max(0, ch.amount_refunded - r.amount);
          ctx.db.update('charge', ch.id, { amount_refunded: total, refunded: total === ch.amount_captured && total > 0 });
        }
      }

      }

    description: A seeded pending refund whose charge is disputed fails with charge_for_pending_refund_disputed when settled, and the charge gets the amount back. Pending refunds on undisputed charges succeed.
    script: |-
      (ctx) => {
        const refunds = ctx.api('GET', '/v1/refunds?limit=100').body.data;
        const pend = refunds.filter((x) => x.status === 'pending');
        const target = pend.find((x) => ctx.api('GET', '/v1/charges/' + x.charge).body.disputed === true);

        const before = ctx.api('GET', '/v1/charges/' + target.charge).body;

        const normal = pend.find((x) => ctx.api('GET', '/v1/charges/' + x.charge).body.disputed === false);

        }
      }
